anchors.name: isPortion
comments: Whether the values of this Feature are contained in the space and time of instances of the domain of the Feature and represent the same thing as those instances.

anchors.name: checkFeaturePortionSpecialization
comments: If a Feature has isPortion = true, an ownedTyping relationship to a Class, and an owningType that is a Class or another Feature typed by a Class, then it must directly or indirectly specialize Occurrences::Occurrence::portions from the Kernel Semantic Library.
bodies: isPortion and ownedTyping.type->includes(oclIsKindOf(Class)) and owningType <> null and (owningType.oclIsKindOf(Class) or  owningType.oclIsKindOf(Feature) and     owningType.oclAsType(Feature).type->         exists(oclIsKindOf(Class))) implies     specializesFromLibrary('Occurrence::Occurrence::portions')

anchors.name: ownedTyping
comments: The ownedSpecializations of this Feature that are FeatureTypings, for which the Feature is the typedFeature.

anchors.name: deriveFeatureOwnedTyping
comments: The ownedTypings of a Feature are its ownedSpecializations that are FeatureTypings.

anchors.name: owningType
comments: The Type that is the owningType of the owningFeatureMembership of this Feature.

anchors.name: deriveFeatureType
comments: The types of a Feature are the union of the types of its typings and the types of the Features it subsets, with all redundant supertypes removed. If the Feature has chainingFeatures, then the union also includes the types of the last chainingFeature.
bodies: type =      let types : OrderedSet(Types) = OrderedSet{self}->         -- Note: The closure operation automatically handles circular relationships.         closure(typingFeatures()).typing.type->asOrderedSet() in     types->reject(t1 | types->exist(t2 | t2 <> t1 and t2.specializes(t1)))

baseline.limits: Compatibility reachability false does not prove complete absence. True explicit/library paths show existing paths, but the checked Feature.type query still refuses all eleven portion Features. These are diagnostic observations, not whole-model validity assertions.

findings: The applicable specialization is conditional: isPortion, an owned FeatureTyping to Class, and an owningType that is Class or a Feature whose effective type includes a Class. Written inherited typing alone is not ownedTyping.

The pinned prose and actual library use Occurrences::Occurrence::portions; the OCL string uses singular Occurrence. Its includes(oclIsKindOf(Class)) predicate and deriveFeatureOwnedTyping ownedGeneralization spelling also conflict with the surrounding property definitions. These discrepancies require a recorded implementation interpretation and remain visible qualification limits.

The existing shared FeatureRequirements explicitly refuses isPortion=true. The public baseline confirms this refusal even for portions with existing direct/transitive library paths. Removing that guard alone would fail to account for conditional required bases.

The executed narrowed owner has effective type Narrow, a Classifier, after redundant Class Owner is pruned. Thus scanning only written Class typing would produce the wrong applicability predicate for its child.

The current shared owner-type certificate is supplied for composite OccurrenceUsage contexts. Portion applicability needs complete effective owner typing under the same work budget and dependency proof; incomplete owner evidence must not become a false predicate. Finite closed typing cycles use the same ordinary closure algorithm.

The library portion and slice Features block Occurrence/Performance self-chain typing, which in turn blocks several selected default result types. Full invocation default binding obligations remain separate.
acceptancePlan: Check exact applicability for Class owners, Features typed directly/inherited by Class, non-Class owners, no owning Type, and a redundant Class pruned from effective owner types.
Distinguish owned Class typing from inherited typing, inverse FeatureTyping relationships and data-only types. Include multiple owned types and nonconforming or unresolved endpoints.

Check required library identity and direct/indirect/self paths. Missing, shadowed or malformed library evidence stays incomplete; an explicit existing path does not excuse incomplete antecedent evidence.
Preserve independent ordinary Feature checks for ownership, flags, metadata, valuation, specialization and role membership. Deliberately damage fresh and previously queried graphs.

Use the shared static planner for required implicit specialization and the same applicability proof for checked readers. Qualify effective owner predicates against the final prospective specialization write set to avoid circular self-justification.

anchors.name: ownedSpecialization
bodies: The ownedRelationships of this Type that are Specializations, for which the Type is the specific Type.

anchors.name: supertypes
bodies: if isConjugated then Sequence{conjugator.originalType} else if not excludeImplied then ownedSpecialization.general else ownedSpecialization->reject(isImplied).general endif endif

If this Type is conjugated, then return just the originalType of the Conjugation. Otherwise, return the general Types from all ownedSpecializations of this type, if excludeImplied = false, or all non-implied ownedSpecializations, if excludeImplied = true.

anchors.name: allSupertypes
bodies: Return this Type and all Types that are directly or transitively supertypes of this Type (as determined by the supertypes operation with excludeImplied = false).

anchors.name: specializes
bodies: if isConjugated then ownedConjugator.originalType.specializes(supertype) else allSupertypes()->includes(supertype) endif
Check whether this Type is a direct or indirect specialization of the given supertype.
